title: DC-area forecast: Less warm today with afternoon shower chances; cool and rainy Tuesday
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Mostly cloudy with comfortable temperatures rising from morning 60s to highs in the low to mid-70s. Isolated to scattered showers are possible this afternoon.

What’s next? Shower chances continue tonight ahead of a rainy, breezy, and cool Tuesday. Rain could linger into early Wednesday before drier weather tries to build in Thursday and Friday. Highs only in the 60s Tuesday and Wednesday should rise later in the week.

Today’s daily digit — 7/10: Hello 70s, goodbye 80s. Lots of clouds, maybe a few showers. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.

Forecast in detail

Today (Monday): The sun may peek through at times, but expect considerable cloud cover throughout the day. The big change is the cooler air, with highs only in the low to mid-70s as light winds come in from the northeast. It's not as humid as over the weekend, but there's still a hint of mugginess, with dew points in the low to mid-60s. Isolated to scattered showers could develop during the afternoon. Confidence: Medium-High

Tonight: Cloudy with intermittent showers that may increase in coverage and frequency toward morning. Lows are around 60, with light winds from the northeast. Confidence: Medium-High

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Tuesday): The first day of fall feels the part with an old-fashioned rainy day. Expect periods of rain, generally light to moderate in intensity, with about half an inch to an inch possible. It's rather breezy, too, with northeast winds around 10 to 15 mph and some gusts over 20 mph. This will probably be our coolest day since May, with highs only 60 to 65. Confidence: Medium-High

Tomorrow night: Periods of rain continue, and it remains cool and breezy. Lows dip into the mid- to upper 50s. Confidence: Medium-High

A look ahead

A little rain could linger into Wednesday morning, but we should start to dry out in the afternoon. It's still cloudy, breezy and cool, with highs in the mid-60s. Partial clearing is possible at night, with lows in the 50s. Confidence: Medium

Mostly dry weather is probable Thursday into Friday as clouds tend to decrease and temperatures warm some. Highs Thursday probably range from the mid-60s to near 70, then rise closer to 70 to 75 Friday. Lows are in the 50s. The lone wrinkle is the possibility of a coastal storm late Friday into early Saturday, but it will probably develop too far north and east to be an issue for the interior Mid-Atlantic. Confidence: Medium

Assuming the storm over the ocean pulls away to the north on Saturday, as expected, the weekend looks quite promising. It should be dry, with highs in the 70s and lows in the 50s. Confidence: Medium

DC weather history for September 21

Heavy rain from a 1979 coastal storm set a daily record and contributed to one of the wetter Septembers on record.
